title: Bartender Techniques for Better Cocktails: Stirring, Shaking, Temperature, and Ice

locations.name: Restaurant downstairs from the office (probable; cited as site of pro tips)
locations.basis: Transcript states that Lan Lam consulted bartenders at the restaurant downstairs from the office; this location is described in-context but not confirmed as the shoot location.

summary: This video breaks down practical bartending techniques into four core areas that influence cocktail quality: stirring, shaking, precise ingredient measurement, and temperature management through glassware and ice. Lan Lam demonstrates a stirred drink (the Little Bologna) to illustrate how generous ice, smooth bar-spoon motion, and proper dilution chill and texture the cocktail; then pivots to shaking with a Sidecar to show aggressive, equipment-driven mixing, straining choices, and aroma effects. The segment on measurement emphasizes reliable pouring and the use of dropper bottles or measuring spoons to achieve balance across spirits, citrus, sweeteners, and bitters. Temperature discussion covers pre-chilled glassware, how to quickly chill a glass, and why serving at the right temperature matters for aroma and perceived sweetness. Finally, the video highlights ice quality—dry, appropriately sized cubes for stirring or shaking, and the impact of wet ice on dilution—along with visual tests of glass temperature and the concept of ‘fridge-door’ cocktails as a prep strategy. Throughout, it anchors tips to the book Cocktails Illustrated and practical demonstrations of recipes like Little Bologna and Sidecars, illustrating how to apply these techniques at home with real tools and measurements.
